source.label: Fitted diameter at the Gaia distance
Uniform-disc fit to the September 2014 VLTI/PIONIER visibilities

controls.label: PIONIER reconstruction
controls.notes: An image of the photosphere reconstructed by the public SQUEEZE code from the public VLTI/PIONIER visibilities and closure phases of four nights in September 2014, in the H band (1.62-1.73 micrometres), convolved to the 2.1 milliarcsecond interferometric beam and cast onto a sphere of the fitted radius, so nothing finer than the beam is shown. The star has no measured rotation axis: the axis shown is celestial north, a display convention. The far hemisphere is unobserved and carries the no-data grid.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Colour from Gaia's spectrum of the star. The disc is unresolved, and no darkening toward the edge is measured.
controls.notes: The colour of Gaia DR3's measured spectrum of π¹ Gruis. At G = 3.6 the star is brighter than the G of about 5 below which Gaia XP photometry can saturate, blue first (Montegriffo et al. 2023, A&A 674, A33), and its RUWE of 2.9 is high, so the blue end of this colour is uncertain. No resolved image of the surface is cast; the display axis is celestial north, a convention.
